response:
No conflicts from my own lane's work, but two real integration risks surfaced in the other reports:

- **Critical: Codex A's proposed entitlements content uses the wrong App Group ID.** Both `Waypoint.entitlements` and `WaypointWidget.entitlements` already exist and are correctly set to `group.com.waypoint.app` — the exact string `WaypointKit/Sources/WaypointKit/AppGroup.swift` defines (`AppGroup.identifier`). Codex A's snippet uses `group.com.yourcompany.waypoint`, a different string. If the integrator applies that snippet as-is, it will silently break the App Group match between the app and widget targets — this is literally the crash class already flagged in DEC-final_review-001. Integrator should diff against the existing files and keep `group.com.waypoint.app`, not overwrite with the placeholder.
- **Severe: Codex B's (Qwen fallback) output re-declares SettingsView, TripSwitcherView, DayView, StopDetailView, TravelerEditView, ExpenseEntryView, and SettleUpView from scratch as non-functional stubs** — hardcoded `.constant("")` text fields, no SwiftData persistence, no validation, no real save logic. These would regress every already-working, already-verified screen in primary_ui's and polish_resilience's builds this round. It also gets the flow contract wrong where it invents identifiers: `expenseEntry.splitMethodPicker` instead of the required `expenseEntry.splitMethodPercentage`, `settings.saveButton` (not a real token), `dayView.listTabButton` (not a real token) — and it's missing `tripEdit.nameField`/`saveButton`, `dayView.stopRow.moveToButton`, `money.addTravelerButton`/`addExpenseButton`/`settleUpButton` entirely. Integrator must not merge any file body from Codex B's report this round — treat it as informational noise, not a diff to apply.
- Claude B's `.secondaryAction` → `.primaryAction` fix on `DayView.swift` (calendarExportButton/moneyButton/packingButton were sinking into iOS's overflow menu, making them unhittable, and moneyButton is the only entry point into the whole Money flow) is a legitimate, correctly-scoped fix to my lane's file and matches what I independently observed reading that file — no objection, just flagging it landed outside its owning lane per DEC-task_assignments-002 conventions, which Claude B already called out themselves.
